results.name: Inside "MR ROBOT" - Anatomy of a Malware-as-a-Service Operation Targeting Indian Bank Customers
results.description: A sophisticated Android Malware-as-a-Service operation called MR ROBOT is actively targeting Indian bank customers through a subscription-based model. The platform enables cybercriminals to rent customized banking trojans distributed via fake Play Store pages and messaging apps. The operation uses a multi-stage dropper that decrypts encrypted payloads to deploy banking trojans capable of intercepting SMS and OTPs, silently enabling call forwarding using the *21# carrier code to bypass phone-based two-factor authentication, and overlaying phishing screens to harvest card details, CVV, ATM PINs, UPI credentials, and identity documents. One tracked affiliate compromised 153 devices and intercepted 5,407 SMS messages across multiple Indian banks. The operation features a Telegram bot storefront offering approximately 36 fake applications impersonating banks, utility providers, and government services, with stolen data exfiltrated to Firebase Realtime Database and Telegram channels.

results.name: Malicious Firefox Extensions Impersonate Phantom, Jupiter, and Bitget to Steal Wallet Secrets
results.description: Three malicious Firefox extensions impersonating popular cryptocurrency wallets—Phantom, Jupiter, and Bitget—were discovered stealing recovery phrases and private keys from users. The extensions use Unicode homoglyphs to mimic legitimate wallet names and route stolen credentials to brand-named subdomains of bonto[.]io. The Phantom impersonator employs a two-stage approach: a loader fetches additional payloads from a remote server at runtime, allowing operators to modify malicious code post-review. All three extensions bundle complete stealers in signed packages that capture seed phrases, private keys, and clipboard data. The campaign uses separate throwaway developer accounts for each listing and provisions infrastructure for additional targets including Coinbase and Exodus wallets. Captured secrets grant attackers complete control over victims' cryptocurrency wallets and assets.

results.name: September 2026 Infostealer Trend Report
results.description: During September 2026, infostealers were primarily distributed through SEO poisoning, disguised as illegal software such as cracks and keygens. Major distribution platforms included Mediafire, AWS S3, Mega, and Cloudflare Storage. EXE files comprised 90.8% of samples, while DLL side-loading accounted for 9.2%, utilizing legitimate files like python37.dll and POWRPROF.dll. A new infostealer named Lzveil, built with Rust, downloads configuration data from C2 servers and uses modified Base64 decryption, XOR encryption, and LZNT1 compression. Email campaigns distributed DarkCloud and AgentTesla infostealers, impersonating construction and logistics companies respectively. Both steal credentials, browser data, cryptocurrency wallets, and system information. The stolen data is often traded on dark web markets or used for secondary attacks.

results.name: Inside Qilin ransomware: ESXi attacks, affiliate networks and double extortion
results.description: Qilin, also known as Agenda, is a Russian-speaking ransomware-as-a-service operation active since 2022 that became one of the most prolific groups by 2025 with over 1,000 claimed victims. The operation employs a flexible platform allowing affiliates to customize attacks targeting local files, network shares, and virtual machine infrastructure. Affiliates typically gain initial access through phishing, stolen credentials, vulnerable internet-facing systems, and remote management tools. The group follows a double-extortion model, encrypting systems while threatening to publish stolen data via their blog and WikiLeaksV2 platform. Notable incidents include the 2024 Synnovis attack affecting UK healthcare services. Qilin has been linked to Moonstone Sleet and Scattered Spider, with some operators creating derivative operations including The Gentlemen and Securotrop, the latter maintaining affiliate status while operating an independent leak site.
targeted_countries: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

results.name: RATatouille: Today's Special: Impersonating Companies in Korea, Payments in Cryptocurrency
results.description: Infrastructure tracking related to ValleyRAT led to the discovery of multiple fraudulent websites impersonating legitimate Korean companies including Doosan Robotics and Cheonjeong. These sites used authentic corporate logos, videos, and descriptions to appear legitimate while offering features like invitation-code registration, VIP memberships, and cryptocurrency deposit/withdrawal functions. Online chat support provided instructions for USDT payments via TRON wallet addresses, requiring users to submit transaction screenshots. Analysis revealed TRON wallet addresses with significant transaction volumes, including one wallet that received approximately 13 million USDT cumulatively. Infrastructure analysis starting from ValleyRAT C2 IP address 14.128.53[.]155 identified 12 potentially associated domains. However, no direct operational connection has been confirmed between ValleyRAT malware operations and these fraudulent websites or cryptocurrency wallets.

results.name: Omegatech Is Disrupted, and the Pressure on Bulletproof Hosting Keeps Building
results.description: The FBI seized virtualine[.]net on October 27, 2026, under Operation Omegaline, targeting Virtualine Technologies, which operated as Omegatech (AS202412). This bulletproof hosting provider emerged in February 2026 after infrastructure shifted from Railnet LLC (AS214943). Bulletproof hosting providers rent servers to cybercriminals while ignoring abuse complaints, enabling phishing, malware, and ransomware operations. Over the past year, 50 such providers lost their autonomous system numbers due to law enforcement action, sanctions, or strategic abandonment. Despite seizures, operators quickly rebrand and acquire new ASNs within days, moving malicious IP ranges to continue operations. Recent enforcement actions include Dutch seizure of THE.Hosting servers, US charges against Russian nationals, and EU sanctions against Media Land. The investigation involved FBI Washington Field Office, Germany's Polizei Hessen, Netherlands' Politie Midden-Nederland, UK's National Crime Agency, and private partners.

results.name: Operation Master: Deconstructing a Multi-Tiered Intrusion and Monetization Pipeline
results.description: A sophisticated cybercrime operation compromised enterprise networks across multiple countries by exploiting a GlobalProtect authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-0257), executed advanced web application attacks, and deployed the AdaptixC2 framework. The operation scanned 277.5 million addresses to curate 81 high-value targets, stole databases from 9+ instances via SQL injection with xp_cmdshell escalation, and exfiltrated Active Directory credentials. Monetization occurred through dual strategies: initially selling corporate and energy sector databases on underground forums under the persona "masterblack", then weaponizing the same data to power a multi-tenant automated invoice fraud platform generating 2.4 million phishing messages and 622,666 personalized fraudulent links. The infrastructure utilized domainless phishing tactics including M365 OAuth device-code phishing and voice-based credential harvesting, collecting payments via PIX through serverless proxies. results.name: Telerik UI Exploitation Leads to Webshell Install and Scanner Execution
results.description: Multiple attack campaigns exploiting CVE-2019-18935, a remote code execution vulnerability in unpatched Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX servers, have been identified. The first case involved exploiting the vulnerability to execute a reverse shell connecting to 206.82.6.22, attempting privilege escalation using Potato-family tools like SweetPotato, and installing a Godzilla-style memory-based web shell that operates within the w3wp.exe process without requiring separate ASPX files. The second case deployed a Rust-based scanner tool that searches for exposed WordPress installation pages across target systems and reports findings via Telegram. Both attacks targeted Windows IIS servers, enabling attackers to maintain persistent access, collect system information, and identify additional targets for future campaigns.

results.name: SkyW4lker Phishing Kit: Microsoft 365 Threat to US Firms
results.description: SkyW4lker is an active device-code phishing kit exploiting Microsoft 365 authentication processes across the United States, Europe, and other regions. Operating since June 2026, it bypasses MFA by abusing legitimate OAuth 2.0 device-code flows, granting attackers access to corporate accounts without stealing passwords. The kit uses phishing emails with password-protected attachments containing links that lead victims through CAPTCHA pages to malicious sites requesting Microsoft device codes. Analysis revealed 618 sandbox submissions between June and October 2026, with 46% originating from US organizations. Monthly activity surged from 20 cases in June to 200 in September. Technical investigation uncovered shared infrastructure and code similarities with the Gabagool credential phishing kit, suggesting common development. The kit employs obfuscated JavaScript, IP-based geolocation, and PHP backends to track victim authentication status, primarily targeting technology, manufacturing, and government sectors.

results.name: Automated Subversion and Attempted Takeover of AI Pentesting Harnesses
results.description: Unprotected Cairn AI intrusion harnesses are being systematically compromised by unknown actors through automated campaigns that began around October 20, 2026. Attackers insert malicious tasks that manipulate agents to compromise the host systems, involving profiling installations, stealing secrets including AI model API keys, downloading Poseidon malware, and installing unauthorized SSH keys. Two distinct threat clusters, designated AIA0009 and AIA0010, conduct synchronized waves of attacks across multiple panels. AIA0009 focuses on persistence and malware deployment, while AIA0010 emphasizes exploration and credential extraction. The campaigns appear highly automated and possibly agentic, utilizing AI to attack AI operations. Activities include container escape attempts, reconnaissance of host environments, and deployment of Poseidon RAT configured with Bunny.net CDN command and control infrastructure.
